report.summary: The failure is a cluster-DNS fault: the CoreDNS configuration in ConfigMap kube-system/coredns contains an injected `template` block that answers NXDOMAIN for exactly `user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local`. As a result compose-post-service cannot resolve `user-service` (Thrift logs `getaddrinfo() <Host: user-service Port: 9090> Name or service not known`, then `(ClientPool.h:114:Pop) Failed to connect user-service-client`), and its caller nginx-thrift returns/reports `ComposePost(): compost_post failure: Could not resolve host for client socket` for every `POST /wrk2-api/post/compose` request from the load client during 14:21:43–14:21:50Z. user-service itself is healthy (Service endpoint 10.244.125.1:9090 present, pod Running/Ready, 0 restarts, only startup log lines, no errors), so the dependency is reachable by IP but not by name — the DNS rule, not the workload, is the fault. A CoreDNS rollout at 14:21:31Z (new ReplicaSet coredns-fc8fb4cf9 replacing coredns-668d6bf9bc, and a `Running configuration SHA512 = ...` reload line at 14:21:32Z) is the mechanism by which the modified Corefile was loaded. What remains unresolved is when/who changed the Corefile (no change-history integration) and DNS-response-level confirmation (no coredns metrics/query logs), so the conclusion is partial while the root cause object is the coredns ConfigMap.

claims.text: ConfigMap kube-system/coredns holds a Corefile whose plugin order is: errors, health, ready, then `template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { match "^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\.$" rcode NXDOMAIN fallthrough }`, then the `kubernetes cluster.local` plugin, prometheus, forward, cache, loop, reload, loadbalance. The injected CoreDNS `template` rule returning NXDOMAIN for user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local is the cause of the resolution failures: bare-name lookups by compose-post-service hit that FQDN first through the pod search path and receive NXDOMAIN, so ComposePost aborts before calling the healthy user-service, and nginx-thrift reports the failure per request.

user-service being down, crashed or having no backing pods is rejected: the Endpoints object has 10.244.125.1:9090, the pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, and its logs show no errors — the failure is name resolution, not endpoint availability.

A pod-level DNS misconfiguration on compose-post-service is rejected: the pod uses dnsPolicy ClusterFirst and declares no dnsConfig nameservers/searches and no hostAliases, so it relies on cluster DNS where the NXDOMAIN rule lives.

CoreDNS itself being unavailable is rejected: both coredns pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts and a clean startup log, and the Corefile's `cache 30 { disable success cluster.local; disable denial cluster.local }` rules mean the NXDOMAIN answers are not negative-cached leftovers.
